NEVER run seeds sync or ml sync in this repo under GitButler; commit .seeds/ and .mulch/ changes explicitly via but commit in the same batch as the code change (fabro iterate precedent).

PR leg until forge auth: gh pr create + gh pr merge --auto --squash (fabro precedent). Local landing NEVER pushes main directly; the workspace follows origin/main with but pull.

Landing: but push + but pr new + but pr auto-merge into main (forge auth valid since 2026-10-03; gh was the interim leg). The workspace follows origin/main with but pull.

description: but pr auto-merge engages auto-merge with merge-method MERGE; main requires linear history — the merge never lands.
resolution: After but pr auto-merge <sel>, ALWAYS re-arm with gh pr merge <n> --auto --squash (PR #3 lesson 2026-10-03: auto-merge enabled at MERGE and stalled silently until re-armed with squash). Recorded in AGENTS.md landing-work bullet.

title: Local iterate sprint system (nu-agent port, but-based, fabro-independent)
rationale: VCS HALF SUPERSEDED 2026-10-17 (mulch-6817): 'use but instead of git' is retired with the GitButler experiment — the loop commits with plain git (batched .seeds/.mulch, lane push through the push gate, PR-only landing to main). The 'fabro-independent' framing was separately corrected 2026-10-06: mulch is STANDALONE and its lib is fabro's native engine (see the lane-push amendment decision). ORIGINAL directive 2026-10-03: work locally for now; same sprint system as nu-agent; the sprint system is independent of the fabro develop line; use but instead of git; delegate worthwhile tasks to subagents.

description: The ml-ref-prober report cited byte sizes (1395/4230) that did not match the actual artifacts (1421/4322) — always pin parity templates from the BYTES (snapshots/files), never from a report transcript; the differential battery against the live reference is the real gate. Resolution: fixtures copied byte-identically from the probe workdir, verified against both snapshots.
resolution: Trust bytes over prose; verify via live differential runs.

title: Architecture gate @ sprint 3: five deepening candidates
rationale: Deepening pays off where the remaining ~20 parity commands each touch the same store; the gate ran after the third sprint as the loop requires.

description: Sprint 4 (mulch-8204): while moving the strict reader behind a lib seam, the first cut dropped the CLI flag that the old call sites passed (`--allow-unknown-types`), so three commands accepted the flag and silently ignored it — a regression the 65-test battery could not see (no test exercised the flag on those commands).
resolution: read_records(domain, allow_unknown) takes the flag explicitly; before/after call-site diff of every flag that reaches a moved function. LESSON: when a function moves behind a seam, diff the ARGUMENTS of every call site, not just the behaviour of the new path.

description: Anchor-based test edits break after `cargo fmt` runs on an uncommitted insert: the formatter rewraps macro args, so exact anchors from the written buffer stop matching the file. Re-read the formatted file region BEFORE constructing the old/new anchor pair (cost: one failed assert in sprint 5).
resolution: Re-read the formatted region before composing anchor pairs; never anchor on unformatted memory of a write.

description: Sprint 6 front-ran part of mulch-ca49 to make the batch envelope differential-testable: added updated/errors/warnings to the batch json envelopes (ccf6's 'reports updated in its counters'). Deliberate, noted in the commit; ca49 keeps the PLAIN surface (Skip:/Create:/Update: lines, Would process count, Skipped N duplicates line, Created 0 line) and the create-only compact rewrite. Rule of thumb: when a parity ticket needs json fields another seed owns, taking the fields is fine IF the commit message says so and the seed stays open for the rest.
resolution: Fields taken deliberately, seed kept open for the plain surface.

title: Sprint-6 architecture gate
rationale: State 6/6 with 6 % 3 == 0 and last review at sprint 3 — the every-3rd-sprint gate is due right after the ccf6 closeout.

description: `seeds update --description` REPLACES the whole description — appending an update requires fetch-current-then-write-full. Hit TWICE in one session (arch-gate reassessments, 00aa probe notes): both times the original text was silently lost and had to be rebuilt from session context. Mitigation: always use a seeds_append helper (show --format json -> current description + addition -> update), never a bare update for addenda.
resolution: Append-only helper bound in the session; consider filing a seeds CLI --description-append feature.

description: Deleting a function by slicing from its doc-comment start to the next `pub fn` can swallow the NEXT function's doc block when anchors drift (sprint 8: read_lines deletion ate read_records' docs; standards review caught it). Deletion guard: after any slice-based delete, grep-verify the SURVIVOR's doc block still sits flush above it — same class as the insert-anchor guard, mirrored for deletions.
resolution: Deletion guard added to the session checklist; iterate skill edit-verification guard already covers region re-reads.

name: expect-over-dead-fallback
description: When a fallback is provably unreachable (e.g. `id().unwrap_or(input)` where the resolver only matches identified records), the code should `expect("invariant")` rather than keep a silent default: the default hides the invariant and can contradict the stated contract (sprint 9 standards review). Mirrored reference JS (`record.id ?? id`) is not a reason to keep dead defaults — name the dead fallback in a comment instead.

name: compare-stderr-too
description: A differential test that compares only STDOUT can pass while the stderr rendering regresses (sprint 10: plain `validate` prints its details on stderr — the const-sub-error spacing bug survived a green battery). Rule: for every command whose details/errors render on stderr, compare stderr too, or say in the test why not (network-bound lines like doctor's update check).

title: retro 2026-10-06: gate recipe, reference-source pointer, match-order rule, seeds json shape
rationale: Retro 2026-10-06 (sprint 15 + arch gate), four loop-asset changes: (1) iterate skill quality gates now default to `timeout 600 just qualitygate` per commit round — the nushell recipe cannot mask a result the way a bash pipe can (two masked gate failures this sprint: cargo build|tail EXIT=0 on a failed build, fmt --check|head FMT_RC=0 on diffs); sprint end keeps one full-workspace nextest battery; raw cargo commands stay owned by AGENTS.md. (2) AGENTS.md carries a one-line pointer to the reference ml TS source (mise where npm:@os-eco/mulch-cli -> node_modules/@os-eco/mulch-cli/src; fallback readlink -f $(command -v ml)) — this session burned ~6 calls rediscovering it. (3) rust-style-guide control-flow: match-arm ORDER is semantics when earlier arms are more specific; merging same-body arms (clippy match_same_arms) must preserve order, pinned by comment+test — clippy's own fix text can reorder arms silently (caught only by a unit test). NOTE: this rule exists ONLY in the repo-local .agents/ copy; the .fabro/skills original lacks it — carry it over on the next drift-refresh or let the fabro line adopt it via its own seed. (4) docs/agents/issue-tracker.md documents the seeds json shapes (single id -> issue, multi -> issues).

title: iterate lane pushes at closeout (amendment 2026-10-06)
rationale: PUSH MECHANIC AMENDED 2026-10-17 (mulch-6817): after the GitButler teardown the closeout push is 'nu .fabro/scripts/push-gate.nu' (exit 0) then 'git push origin iterate' in the same unpiped cell; everything else in this decision stands. CORRECTED FRAMING (user correction 2026-10-06 evening, same day as the amendment): mulch is a STANDALONE tool — the mulch CLI is its own product — while crates/mulch (the lib) is simultaneously the native expertise engine denkhaus/fabro embeds. The iterate loop is mulch's OWN development loop, not a satellite of the fabro develop line; 'independence from fabro' was the wrong frame. What stays: lane pushes to origin/iterate at every sprint closeout (push gate, exit 0, then the push) for cross-machine availability — pushing the branch is not landing; PRs/main integration stay explicit-user-order-only (engine flow). NEW consequence of the corrected framing: the lib's public API is an integration surface for fabro — lib API changes are integration-relevant and deserve that lens in review (the standalone-tool-plus-embedded-crate posture now also sits in README's Product posture paragraph).

title: Two surgical iterate-loop changes after sprints 19-21: commit-integrity check (but status under-reports; verify the committed file list) and reviewer-handoff git hashes
rationale: BOTH SURVIVE in plain-git form after the GitButler teardown (2026-10-17, mulch-6817): the integrity check now lists intended files with git status --short + git diff --name-only, stages explicit paths and verifies the landed list with git show --stat <hash>; reviewers are always handed resolvable git hashes (git log --grep=<seed> --format=%h -1) — the unresolvable-but-commit-id half of the problem retired with the tool. ORIGINAL (sprints 19-21): both frictions cost real work in consecutive sprints: sprint 20 shipped a commit whose message claimed 7/7 collapsed sites while the worktree change to records.rs never entered the commit (but status hid the file), and sprint-20/21 reviewers each lost time resolving a but-commit id that git cannot show. The rest of the loop held (both review gates caught real issues, probe-first paid off in sprint 19).

title: Multi-seed sprints run as parallel subagents on GitButler lanes above iterate
rationale: MECHANISM SUPERSEDED 2026-10-17 (mulch-6817): the GitButler lanes are retired — the protocol now runs all chain links as SIMULTANEOUS subagents in ONE worktree with DISJOINT file ownership, and the HOST commits each delivery (git add <that child's paths> && git commit, one commit per child; children never touch git). Unchanged: the user directive to run chain links as simultaneous subagents, host-folded shared files, host-side fmt/clippy/battery gates, read-only reviewers. ORIGINAL (user directive 2026-10-11): work with subagents and use GitButler for simultaneous work in the same codebase. Sprint 22 proved the protocol for one crate + big battery: three chain links, three lanes, zero cross-lane incidents.

title: Host pre-lands shared seams before spawning parallel lanes
rationale: Sprint 23: the failure_envelope constructor was the only edge between lane A and lane B; pre-landing it removed the dependency for the cost of one small host commit.

title: The shipped binary carries no ml references: it promotes mulch everywhere (prime and Retry echo included); ml stays the working tool + reference until feature parity
rationale: mulch replaces ml at the self-hosting cutover (mulch-96ed); any user-facing text promoting the retired binary works against that. ml stays in use as tool+reference only during the parity phase, which is process, not binary output.

content: Long 'but commit -m' strings get mangled by the shell (backticks inside double quotes run command substitution — sprint 25 lost the pup message's quoted parts and needed a reword). Rule: long commit messages go through a file — write /tmp/msg.txt, commit with -m "$(cat /tmp/msg.txt)", verify the landed message with but show <id> (the commit-integrity check already demands listing intended files before and git show --stat after).

title: ORIENT checks lane staleness before trusting the worktree
rationale: STILL IN FORCE; mechanism changed with the GitButler teardown 2026-10-17 (mulch-6817): git fetch, then compare .iterate-state.json against the lane's top commit message, then git rebase origin/iterate (never with a dirty worktree or a background cargo running). The but-era catch-up dance (unapply sibling lanes / but branch update / re-apply) is gone with the tool. ORIGINAL (sprint 29): but status no-changes does not imply a current worktree — another machine may have moved origin/iterate; the catch-up dance (unapply sibling lanes, update, re-apply non-colliding) failed twice before succeeding in sprint 29

description: GitButler cross-machine lane catch-up (mulch, 2026-10-15): origin/iterate had moved 4 sprints on another machine while this workspace stayed applied at the old tip — but status parsed fine and showed "no changes", so the stale worktree only surfaced via .iterate-state.json disagreeing with the lane commits. Direct `but branch update iterate` FAILED: "Failed to merge bases while cherry picking <workspace commit> ... conflict ... 17fb074, cb4f325" — the workspace merge commit could not be rebuilt because a SECOND applied lane (chore/but-fork-6) touches .mise.toml lines adjacent to origin/iterate additions (fused hunk collision; the but fork.6/fork.7 patches addressed this class but the workspace-commit cherry-pick still dies). Working dance: `but unapply <other-lane>` then `but branch update iterate` (succeeds instantly), leaving the other lane UNAPPLIED — its re-apply collides with the new base (adjacent .mise.toml lines), so the pin content must land on the moved base or the lane waits for a rebased duplicate. ORIENT rule: compare the state file against the lane commits BEFORE trusting the worktree; never assume but status healthy = worktree current.
resolution: unapply the colliding sibling lane (chore/but-fork-6), but branch update iterate, keep the sibling unapplied until its mise pin lands on the moved base; ORIENT now checks state-file-vs-lane-commit staleness first (skill change sprint 29)

title: Sprint notes rotate out of the state file
rationale: The notes array grows one long entry per sprint and every session start reads the whole state file; brightctl hit the 50-KB read-tool limit at 222 notes. Rotation keeps the working set small while the JSONL archive stays git-diffable history.

name: gitbutler-remote-rewrite-conflict-discard
description: RETIRED 2026-10-17 (GitButler teardown, mulch-6817) — kept as history: the tool, 'but branch update' and the oplog 'but discard' no longer exist. ORIGINAL RECIPE: When another machine history-edits the pushed lane (split/rebase of a commit that exists locally, e.g. a squashed sprint commit re-split remotely), but branch update <lane> integrates the remote stack and leaves the stale LOCAL duplicate {conflicted} atop it. Resolution: verify the local commit's content is contained in the remote stack (diff local-commit vs the remote code-equivalent commit; patch-id --stable on crates/ if bases differ), then 'but discard <commit-id>' (oplog-undoable) — never resolve hunk-by-hunk, the workspace already carries the newer work. The partial conflict overlay can leave a non-compiling mix in the worktree until the discard rebuilds it. WHAT SURVIVES: before integrating a moved remote branch, prove containment first (diff / patch-id --stable) and take the REMOTE side — under plain git that is commit-or-stash, then git fetch + git rebase origin/<branch>.

title: Hunk IDs come from but status -fv
rationale: RETIRED 2026-10-17 (mulch-6817): but is gone — the hunk-id collection problem does not exist under plain git, which stages by PATH, not by hunk id. The lesson that survives is the commit-integrity check: list intended files first (git status --short + git diff --name-only), stage explicit paths, verify the landed list with git show --stat <hash>. ORIGINAL (2026-10-17): three times in one session a multi-hunk file's ID set was under-collected by grepping but diff's box headers — the wrapped box layout hides headers; the integrity check had to catch each miss via amend. but status -fv lists hunk IDs per file reliably.

content: Plain-git VCS conventions (GitButler retired 2026-10-17, mulch-6817 — supersedes the five but-era variants mx-bc4df7/mx-a883c3/mx-9af32f/mx-dc1a6d/mx-4d91cf): (1) PUSH = 'nu .fabro/scripts/push-gate.nu' (exit 0) then 'git push origin <branch>' in the SAME unpiped cell — never pipe the gate (a piped exit code is the pipe member's; fabro 2026-10-02 incident); (2) local landing NEVER pushes main directly: 'gh pr merge <n> --auto --squash' (main requires linear history), the local lane follows origin/main with git fetch + git rebase; (3) commit .seeds/ and .mulch/ explicitly in the SAME commit as the change they document — seeds sync/ml sync open their own commits, so they stay out of the batch flow (seeds sync --status / --dry-run is the pending-change check); (4) long commit messages go through a file (git commit -F /tmp/msg.txt) — inline -m strings with quotes/backticks get shell-mangled (sprint 25); (5) the one-time empty root commit 235a70d was a gitbutler bootstrap exception, now historical — no content ever landed that way.

name: ml-record-upsert-anatomy
description: How to amend mulch's own expertise records (learned 2026-10-17, mulch-6817): ml record upserts ONLY at the type's dedup key — pattern=name, decision=reference=guide=title, convention=content, failure=description. NAMED types replace in place (outcomes merged, EVERY other field replaced — re-pass title/tags/evidence or they are lost). ANONYMOUS types SKIP on duplicate: a changed content/description is a NEW record, and --force pushes a second copy instead of replacing. So a stale CONVENTION can never be amended — record a superseding one with --supersedes <old ids> (ml search renders it as [supersedes: ...]), which is why operational rules you expect to amend should live as pattern/decision records.

name: parallel-reviewers-spawn-via-pig-p
description: The iterate loop's PARALLEL reviewer subagents spawn non-interactively as 'pig -p <prompt>' — one process per axis, both started in ONE cell, outputs captured to files, each under timeout 600. The claude CLI -p channel was unusable 2026-10-17 (credit balance too low). Probe hygiene from the iterate skill applies: pass the diff INLINE in the prompt (bounded; the diff needs no tool use), forbid writes/commits in the prompt text, collect both replies before aggregating. Evidence: sprint mulch-6817 ran both axes this way (standards + spec, 400-word caps held).

title: iterate is a skill, not a branch: the loop works directly on main (user directive 2026-10-17)
rationale: User directive 2026-10-17, same session as the mulch-6817 doc rework: drop the separate "iterate" BRANCH — the loop commits directly on "main", and "iterate" names only the SKILL (.agents/skills/iterate/SKILL.md). Executed: fast-forwarded main onto the sprint-33 tip, deleted the local branch, then deleted origin/iterate; AGENTS.md (Version control, Iterate-loop, push-gate step), the skill (intro, MAIN-staleness check, closeout push, host pre-land) and ADR-0001 decision 2 were reworded (0002b00). Push policy that follows: git push origin main through the two-layer gate, fast-forward only (git fetch + git pull --ff-only first); run PRs stay the engine's path, this loop opens none. Consequence: with no lane, staleness is read off origin/main's top commit vs .iterate-state.json.

title: The state notes ARE the handoff: no HANDOFF.md (user directive 2026-10-17)
rationale: User directive 2026-10-17: the source of ALL issues is seeds, not a handoff file. HANDOFF.md had no prescribing rule anywhere (AGENTS/skill never mentioned it — pure session habit over 6 commits), its Next-steps duplicated the state notes' trailing NEXT: lines, its status sections were a stale cache of AGENTS.md/skill, and its issues were already seeds (mulch-16da, mulch-e2df) or derivable (arch gate = 33 % 3 vs last_arch_review_at_sprint). Removed in f223209 after rescuing the two knowledge bits that existed nowhere else (mulch-compat reference-probe-config-quoted-version, rust rust-line-continuation-eats-indent). The iterate skill now states the invariant: four homes only — seeds = issues, state notes = session state + NEXT, mulch = knowledge, AGENTS/skill = rules. Transient state (push pending) is derived at ORIENT via git fetch + the gate, never stored.

description: Inline double-quoted CLI arguments run embedded backticks AS COMMANDS (hit 2026-10-17 at session close): an ml record --rationale "..." with backticked words executed main (an unrelated Go CLI - its log lines were spliced INTO the record), expanded backticked iterate to empty (command not found), and RAN backticked git fetch, git pull --ff-only and git push origin main as side effects. The push went out WITHOUT the push gate (it reported "Everything up-to-date" so nothing landed, and the gate had been open moments earlier - but the explicit gate step was skipped). Both decision records were corrupted and had to be re-upserted from files. RECURRENCE (sprint 52): the same trap on ml record --description - a backticked example named an editor binary, so a mailcap command ran (harmless there) and the stored text silently lost that clause; caught by reading the record back. The rule had only named --reason/--rationale, so the flag list was too narrow.
resolution: Any long or quoted argument goes through a file: git commit -F, and --reason / --rationale / --description / --files as "$(cat /tmp/x.txt)" (single expansion - content is never re-evaluated, so backticks stay literal). Single-quoted arguments are safe for text without embedded single quotes; prefer the file. Self-check: a backtick inside any double-quoted shell argument is command substitution - if you did not mean to run it, quote it from a file. ALWAYS read a recorded record back (ml search or the jsonl) when its text mattered: the upsert-by-name repair is cheap, a silently truncated record is not noticed later.

name: arch-gate-probe-children-recipe
description: Arch-gate recipe that worked twice (gate @33, 2026-10-18, 6 candidates): (1) scope from `git log <last-gate-closeout>..HEAD` hot spots + the NEXT chain step's surfaces; (2) ONE read-only explorer child with the codebase-design vocabulary, the previous gate's candidate outcomes (do-not-re-suggest), the open-seed list, and a /tmp/<gate>/findings.md deliverable + a <=15-line reply; (3) for probes, parallel probe children per topic delivering /tmp/<sprint>/<topic>-probes/LAW.md with RAW bytes + fixture stores kept in place (they become the wave's differential fixtures); (4) HTML report on a localhost port reserved beforehand (ss -tlnH check), agent-browser-verified (`agent-browser eval` SVG count, not a visual glance) — never xdg-open/file path (user policy); (5) every non-Speculative candidate becomes a seed IMMEDIATELY (Strong and Worth exploring alike) with the explorer's file list + deletion-test verdict; Speculative ones stay report-referenced; (6) chain in the state note, deps wired where the candidates genuinely block the next wave.

title: iterate step-1 ticket annotation: use --append-description (skill fix, 2026-10-18)
rationale: Sprint-34 session close (2026-10-18): the arch gate @33 ran as a chain (explorer child -> two probe children -> report on localhost:4401 + 5 seeds), then sprint 34's three prep folds landed gate-green (6831 3392f65, bb38 8852cdd, 27ec 1393a58) — reviews not yet run, so the session CLOSED EARLY on user order with a handoff seed (mulch-5659) carrying the state. THE SKILL CHANGE from this session's reflection: step-1's ticket-annotation flag was wrong (`--description` does not exist; the real flags are --append-description/--set-description/--replace-in-description) — one failed call, corrected in .agents/skills/iterate/SKILL.md so future sessions do not rediscover it. Everything else this session (render/corpus laws, clippy shapes, probe-child recipe) is captured in mulch, not in the loop.

description:
Ungated pushes of main observed (2026-10-18): `git reflog show origin/main` recorded three 'update by push' entries matching THIS loop's commits (d25df9e, 3392f65, 8852cdd) while the loop never ran `git push` in that session. The two commits after them (1393a58, b6fbe67) stayed local — so the pushes stopped when the session stopped changing HEAD, i.e. they were tied to commit activity in this checkout, not to the loop's closeout step.
What it is NOT (checked): scripts/qualitygate.nu has no push; the only .nu push is .fabro/scripts/dup-run-check-fixtures.nu, sandboxed to a mktemp bare origin; no but/GitButler process; the only git hook is the lefthook pre-push wrapper; .git/config keeps gitbutler.project.* leftovers.
Consequence: the push-gate discipline cannot be assumed to hold for main (AGENTS.md's two layers) — an external actor attached to the checkout pushes main. Detection available to the loop: `git reflog show origin/main` (entries read 'update by push' — a local push, not a fetch). ORIENT's staleness check currently compares origin/main's TIP against the state file; extend it to read the origin/main reflog when a push the loop did not make is suspected. Seed: mulch-4e95.
resolution: Identify the pusher (operator/automation outside the loop) and route it through the push gate or remove it; the loop detects such pushes via `git reflog show origin/main` (local 'update by push' entries), not by its own push bookkeeping.

description:
Ungated pushes of main observed (2026-10-18): `git reflog show origin/main` recorded three 'update by push' entries matching THIS loop's commits (d25df9e, 3392f65, 8852cdd) while the loop never ran `git push` in that session. The commits after them (1393a58, b6fbe67) stayed local until the loop's own gated closeout push — so those pushes stopped when HEAD stopped moving, not at the loop's closeout step.
Ruled out: scripts/qualitygate.nu has no push; the only .nu push is .fabro/scripts/dup-run-check-fixtures.nu, sandboxed to a mktemp bare origin; no GitButler/`but` process (but RETIRED for this repo since 2026-10-17 — the gitbutler.* config keys and .git/gitbutler were dead relics, removed at close 2026-10-18, so they were never the actor); the only git hook is the lefthook pre-push wrapper, which fires ON a push and cannot cause one.
Consequence: the push-gate discipline cannot be assumed to hold for main (AGENTS.md's two layers) — an external actor attached to the checkout pushes main. ORIENT's staleness check compares origin/main's tip against the state file; extend it to read the origin/main reflog when a loop-foreign push is suspected. Seed: mulch-4e95.
resolution: Identify the pusher (operator/automation outside the loop) and route it through the push gate or remove it; the loop detects such pushes via `git reflog show origin/main` (local 'update by push' entries), not by its own push bookkeeping.

title: Three seeds per sprint
rationale: Sprints bundle at least THREE seeds each — the review overhead of a sprint (two reviewer axes + gates + closeout) is fixed, so one-seed sprints review more than they build. Plan main seed + same-family riders (preps, folds, small bugs) at ORIENT. Big waves count as one of the three.

title: English-only artifacts
rationale: Every durable artifact is ENGLISH ONLY: code comments, doc comments, commit messages, seeds texts, mulch records. Session conversation may stay German; the repo's memory may not. Applies to subagent prompts and deliveries too.

title: Pre-land only pub constructors in parallel chains
rationale: Children cannot run workspace gates, so a pre-land commit must pass the host's clippy -D warnings alone — only `pub` lib items are exempt from dead-code; CLI-side helpers ride the adopting child's delivery instead.

title: Host-only sprints are viable when the quota blocks children
rationale: With the subagent quota blocked (429), sprint 40 ran host-only: compact (8a1b), init .gitattributes (6546), raw summaries (f06a) — three seeds, sequential host delivery, host review. Worked because the seeds were probe-first scoped and the batteries are differential (no expected-bytes authoring). Children are an optimization, not a requirement; the review axes ran as a host pass with the deviation recorded in the sprint note.

name: child death at a usage limit: re-verify the WIP, do not trust it
description: Parallel children that hit a provider usage limit leave their in-place edits in the tree (children never touch git, so nothing is lost). The host must treat that WIP as unreviewed: run the child batteries first, then read every diff before integrating. Sprint 42: three of the four red tests were test-authoring bugs in the children batteries (an unterminated concat! literal, a retain() that stripped a flag value, a byte-compare across two independently seeded stores), and only one was a real regression (the unlocked config write) - the code under test was sound in all four. Budget the takeover as verification work, not rework. SECOND SHAPE (mulch-d5c3, sprint 52): the child can also end MID-FLIGHT - a bare completed-without-a-text-response, no delivery note, no decision tables, and an unrepaired call site left calling a function the child had deleted. Inventory checklist before continuing: git status, diff --stat per child-owned file, the note path the brief named, and a cargo check - a missing note is the signal that the delivery contract was not met.

title: A new seam gets a decision-table module test, not only parity batteries
rationale: Sprint 43 (mulch-c7ca) folded eight hook call sites onto HookPhase and the parity suite proved every moved behaviour — but the adapter's own laws went untested: blocked_reason's three arms (engine reason, empty reason beating the fallback because JS `??` is nullish-only, and the fallback itself) and the falsy adoption rows (false/0/"") only got tests after both reviewers asked for them. Rule added to .agents/skills/iterate/SKILL.md: when a sprint introduces an adapter or newtype, pin every enum arm and every fallback law at the module level in the same commit — moved-behaviour batteries are necessary, not sufficient. Companion measures that made the seam hold: #[must_use] on the phase and the decision enum, private internals so consumers cannot bypass the ritual.

title: Consolidation claims are counted; new pins must be seen red against the naive form
rationale: Sprint 44 (mulch-593e) produced two review findings of the same shape. ADR-0004 claimed 'one atomicity owner' for StoreFiles while rewrite_archive still carried its own pid-less temp+rename - the claim was written from the intent, not from a grep. And the new store test asserted 'no scratch file left behind', which a plain fs::write also satisfies, so the sprint's headline win (atomicity) had zero coverage until a hard-link witness was added (old inode keeps old bytes) and verified RED against a patched in-place rewrite. Rule added to .agents/skills/iterate/SKILL.md: before writing a consolidation claim, grep for the copies of the mechanism in the same cell; before trusting a pin, name the wrong implementation it catches and watch it fail against that implementation. Corollary that also held: an assertion of absence is rarely discriminating - assert the mechanism's observable signature instead.

title: Attribution claims are probed against the reference source, never remembered from port code
rationale: Sprint 45 (mulch-a2c9) review caught the ADR and commit message calling stamp_id 'the exact reference generateRecordId port' while the reference (utils/expertise.ts:113-120) actually THROWS for unregistered types - the port's 'content' fallback had lived in the command copy so long it read as parity. The lesson generalizes the sprint-44 counting rule: a consolidation claim is COUNTED (grep the copies), and a reference-behaviour claim is PROBED (read the reference file:line in the same session, cite it in the doc). Port code is evidence of what the PORT does, never of what the reference does - no matter how old and authoritative the port copy looks. Corollary: when a move preserves such a deviation byte-neutrally, the docs of the new home must label the deviation explicitly, and any live divergence surface gets a seed instead of a silent inheritance.

name: Three-agent sprint review: standards, spec, and an adversarial code revisor
description: User directive 2026-10-25, proven in sprint 46: after every sprint run THREE parallel subagents - standards (rust-style-guide + repo conventions), spec (seed/ADR delivery + parity bytes), and a CODE REVISOR whose only job is weaknesses: latent bugs, edge cases, risky assumptions, untested paths, and behavior changes the commit did not name, with reference-binary probes as its sharpest tool. Sprint 46's proof: both classic axes returned PASS-with-nits while the revisor found the 2809 fix errored at the WRONG SITE (reference dies at candidate collection, not the merge), that the port printed output the reference never printed, and that multi-domain stores were partially compacted before the error - all three folded into eb6cfdd. The revisor prompt explicitly disclaims standards and spec ('two other reviewers cover those') and permits throwaway probes under /tmp/opencode but never repo writes. Prompt shape that worked: list the attack surfaces as questions (overflow conversions, test-consolidation losses, write ordering vs the error site, mode coverage, unannounced API growth), demand [bug]/[risk]/[gap]/[observation] labels with file:line evidence.

title: Three-agent sprint review: standards, spec, and an adversarial code revisor
rationale: CORRECTED 2026-10-25 (user clarification): the post-sprint review is the code-review SKILL - exactly one invocation, whose own two built-in subagents run the standards and spec axes in parallel. Nothing additional: the 'code revisor' the user asked for IS that skill, not a third agent. Sprint 46 misread this as pair-PLUS-revisor (three agents, two redundant; the misread was itself folded into the skill and amended the same day). What survives from the sprint-46 experience: (a) the two-axis separation itself (a change can pass standards and fail spec, and vice versa - report separately, never rerank across axes); (b) the sharpened spec brief - where a diff claims REFERENCE behaviour, verify the site and ordering against the reference source (the 2809 lesson: an error at a different site than the reference's crash point changed stdout and produced a partially written store); (c) read-only reviewer subagents with bounded reads and timeout on every command, findings as the reply, the host commits.

name: A closed seed's claimed scope can be narrower than its family - verify the 'last X' claim
description: mulch-1c32's sprint-48 fold claimed 'the last string dispatch of the format family' after enum-izing the ENVELOPE - but prime's manifest, contract and session-close families still matched &str (five more match sites, plus an undocumented 5th format name 'embedded' only session-close knows). The spec review caught it because it compared the CLAIM against the SEED's wording ('Format::envelope as the table's owner' was one of two named tables). Rule: when a consolidation seed names N sites and the implementation lands N-1, the commit message must say which landed and which did not - and 'the last X' claims are grep-verified in the same cell before writing them (the sprint-44 counting rule, applied to negations). Corollary: a re-scope claim without a filed seed is a claim, not a delivery - the same review caught 're-scoped into a follow-up seed' with no seed existing; file first, then commit the reference.

Sprint 49 (mulch-3e3b): while fixing a corrupted string-splice in ONE file, `git checkout -- crates/mulch/src/commands/` restored the whole commands/ tree - silently reverting the sprint's D1+D2 work (Format threading, golden tables) in uncommitted siblings. The next commit's message described the full delivery; the tree contained none of it. Detection came ONLY from the two-axis code review (standards: 'commit describes work not in the commit'; spec: zero new tests, format.rs untouched).
resolution: Recovered by restoring the work, AMENDING the commit with the incident documented, and re-running both axes on the amended tree (PASS, 485 tests). Rules now in the iterate skill: (1) never scope a checkout wider than the file being repaired; (2) after ANY restore, grep the sprint's claimed surfaces and run its new tests before committing; (3) the test-count delta is part of commit-message verification (477 stayed 477 while the message claimed 485); (4) amend-don't-append when the original message is materially false - history must not preserve a lie.

content:
Pace reports cite `seeds stats --pace` as the STANDARD source: closure rate (30d + all-time), pace k, median lead time, median open age, open-to-target, ETA verdict, and the weekly created/closed/open series. The `seeds prime` header carries only a subset of these (rate, k, open-to-target) and is not a pace report; manual git-log archaeology (closeout-date counting) is not one either.

Supplementing is allowed only for metrics seeds does not have — e.g. sprints/day has no seeds metric, so git-derived sprint cadence may be shown, but must be labeled as git-derived.

Origin: user directive 2026-10-26 — a feature-completeness/pace overview cited prime's header line plus hand-computed git-log cadence instead of the dedicated stats command.

When one file carries two seeds changes (sprint 53: store.rs held the 7112 view seam and the 73b5 write seam), keep one commit per seed by staging the shared file at an INTERMEDIATE version for the first commit: seam A present, seam B absent, seam B callers unstaged at HEAD. The first commit tree then compiles (HEAD callers still use the old API); restore the full file and commit the second seed with its callers. Verify every commit with git show --stat; a working-tree cargo check failing against the intermediate state is EXPECTED (it sees unstaged callers). Slice the file by asserted line markers, never blind index math (a wrong cut left a stray brace once). git add -p is interactive and not an alternative.

title: Arch gate @ 54: C1 Failure ctors filed Strong, C2-C4 filed, C5 parked
rationale: Gate @ 54 (explorer over f0a481d..HEAD, report http://localhost:8793/architecture-review-54.html, agent-browser-verified: 6 sections, 5 badges): the sprints-52-54 cycle consolidated the alias law end-to-end (write guard, addressing table, read-view merge), the two-open ritual (3 callers folded), the git process adapter, and sync - all landed where the ADRs put them. What the gate found is the NEXT consolidation layer: unnamed output laws and walk skeletons that the parity wave has been re-spelling per command.

title: Sprint state carries sprint objects; rust-security review every 5th sprint
rationale: User directive 2026-10-26: port fabro iterate-state.json structure. The flat notes array (one string per note, gates and corrections floating between sprint numbers) became sprints: [{"sprint": N, "notes": [...]}] - a sprint can carry several notes, the record doubles as its own archive row, and new fields ride along without touching the rotation script. Two cadence fields added: last_code_review_at_sprint (every sprint, seeded 54) and last_rust_security_review_at_sprint (every 5th, starts null -> first due at 55). Rotation keeps the newest 10 SPRINTS, archives ONE {"sprint","notes"} JSON line per sprint (dedup by sprint id, archive-before-state write). Archive migrated: 61 note lines -> 45 sprint records (0-44); state holds 45-54.

content: Every grilling question in the iterate loop is a structured selection via the question tool (user directive 2026-10-26, same rule fabro adopted): the RECOMMENDED option first - labelled "(Recommended)" - then the real alternatives, multiple: true where choices combine, "Type your own answer" rides along automatically. Free-text question lists in chat are OUT. Chat carries the context AROUND a question (why it is load-bearing, the frontier); the question tool carries the question itself. Rationale: overview - one place to answer, one click per decision, the recommendation visible before the alternatives. Applies to every load-bearing decision the loop puts to the user: seed-bundle exceptions, direction gates, arch-candidate order, deviation approvals.
